population_detail: >=35 weeks at risk of hypoglycaemia (IDM, preterm, SGA, LGA, acute illness)
intervention: hypoglycaemia treated to maintain BG>=2.6 mmol/L (47 mg/dL)
outcomes_measured: neurosensory impairment; processing difficulty (Bayley-III, executive function, motion coherence) at 2y
secondary_results: unrecognised (interstitial-only) hypoglycaemia, lowest glucose, episode number, negative interstitial increment all non-predictive
ascertainment_method: masked continuous interstitial glucose monitoring + intermittent blood glucose
grade_reason: imprecision (wide CIs); no untreated comparator possible
funding: Eunice Kennedy Shriver NICHD and others
key_limitation: single-centre; treat-to-threshold design cannot inform untreated natural history
notes: CHYLD study 2-year primary outcome; null result given equal prominence per brief rule
glucose_measurement_method: mixed (intermittent blood glucose + masked continuous interstitial)

outcomes_measured: combined neurosensory impairment; executive function; visual-motor function at 4.5y
primary_result: null for composite; positive for executive & visual-motor function
secondary_results: highest risk with severe, recurrent (>=3 episodes), or clinically undetected (interstitial-only) hypoglycaemia - dose-response
ascertainment_method: masked continuous interstitial glucose monitoring + intermittent blood glucose
grade_reason: imprecision (wide CI on executive function RR); indirectness (single cohort)
key_limitation: domain-specific not global effect; single cohort
notes: CHYLD 4.5-year follow-up; central dose-response finding for this domain
glucose_threshold_used: 2.6 mmol/L / 47 mg/dL; severe <2.0 mmol/L / 36 mg/dL; recurrent >=3 episodes
glucose_measurement_method: mixed (intermittent blood glucose + masked continuous interstitial)

population_detail: moderate-late preterm and term at risk of hypoglycaemia
outcomes_measured: low educational achievement (reading/maths) at 9-10y; 47 secondary outcomes
secondary_results: teacher-rated reading below curriculum LOWER in exposed group (24% vs 31%, aRD -9%, 95% CI -17 to -1, aRR 0.72, p=.04) - likely multiplicity/chance given 47 secondary comparisons; all other secondary outcomes non-significant
grade_reason: imprecision; single cohort (indirectness re: unselected term population)
key_limitation: counter-intuitive secondary finding most likely a multiplicity artefact, not causal
notes: CHYLD 9-10 year academic achievement outcome; second null primary result at later timepoint

population_detail: >=36 weeks at risk of hypoglycaemia, MRI subset at 9-10y
outcomes_measured: caudate volume (FreeSurfer) vs executive function, academic achievement, emotional-behavioural regulation
primary_result: caudate volume associated with emotional-behavioural difficulties and prosocial behaviour; no significant caudate x hypoglycaemia interaction on main outcomes
effect_size: not a single pooled effect size (regression/interaction study)
p_value: interaction p=0.03 for visual memory (unexposed only)
secondary_results: hypoglycaemia associated with smaller caudate volume (from prior work) but this did not explain behavioural/cognitive associations in this analysis
directness: direct - late preterm/term at-risk population, MRI subset
key_limitation: structural correlate not yet mechanistically linked to behavioural findings - parallel finding, not explanatory
notes: Structural correlate; explicitly flagged in brief as needing clarity on whether it explains behavioural findings - it does not, per this paper

population_detail: late preterm and term at risk of hypoglycaemia, pooled CHYLD/Sugar Babies/hPOD-programme cohorts
outcomes_measured: Bayley motor/cognitive/language, BRIEF global executive composite at 2y, by continuous vs dichotomous glycaemic measures
primary_result: dichotomous severe/recurrent hypoglycaemia more strongly predictive than continuous variability measures
effect_size: -3.1 (severe) vs -2.1 (recurrent) vs -0.9 (per 1SD gradient variability) adjusted mean Bayley motor score
secondary_results: associations similar for cognitive, language, and executive composite scores
ascertainment_method: intermittent capillary blood glucose, multiple derived continuous and dichotomous measures
grade_reason: very recent single analysis (2026), not yet independently replicated; indirectness of variability metrics not previously validated
key_limitation: first head-to-head test of variability vs threshold measures in this evidence base - open rather than closed question per authors
notes: Directly addresses brief's Domain D glycaemic-variability question, though this cohort is late-preterm/term not preterm
glucose_threshold_used: severe <2.0 mmol/L/36 mg/dL; recurrent >=3 episodes; treated to >=2.6 mmol/L/47 mg/dL

population_detail: >=35 weeks, confirmed hypoglycaemia <2.6 mmol/L in first 48h
secondary_results: high absolute rate of impairment in BOTH arms (36% overall: 1 severe, 6 moderate, 59 mild) reflecting underlying risk-factor burden, not gel effect
ascertainment_method: Bayley-III, BRIEF-P, clinical exam, motion coherence
directness: direct - late preterm/term with confirmed hypoglycaemia
key_limitation: high baseline impairment rate not attributable to gel allocation
notes: Sugar Babies trial 2-year follow-up (treatment, not prophylaxis)

outcomes_measured: neurosensory impairment at 4.5y; visual processing; growth
secondary_results: dextrose arm WORSE visual processing scores (94.5 vs 99.8, p=0.02); dextrose arm taller (z 0.18 vs -0.17, p=0.001) and heavier (z 0.57 vs 0.29, p=0.01)
ascertainment_method: Beery VMI, motion coherence, MABC-2, WPPSI
grade_reason: imprecision - visual processing is a secondary outcome not powered as primary
notes: Adverse visual-processing signal given equal prominence to reassuring primary null per brief rule

outcomes_measured: low educational achievement; visual perception; executive function at 9-10y
secondary_results: dextrose arm LOWER visual perception scores (95.2 vs 100.6, MD -5.68, 95% CI -9.79 to -1.57, p=0.006) and more scoring <85 (23% vs 11%, RR 2.23, 95% CI 1.13-4.37, p=0.02) - replicates 4.5y signal
grade_reason: imprecision (secondary outcome); though now replicated across two timepoints in same trial
key_limitation: mechanism for visual-processing signal unknown; replicated across 4.5y and 9-10y in same trial
notes: Visual-processing adverse signal now replicated at two timepoints - given equal prominence to null primary result

population_detail: late preterm and term at risk of hypoglycaemia, well at 1h of age
outcomes_measured: neurosensory impairment at 2y; 44 secondary outcomes (Bayley-III composites)
secondary_results: dextrose arm HIGHER motor delay (2.5% vs 0.7%, aRR 3.79, 95% CI 1.27-11.32) and LOWER cognitive (aMD -1.30), language (aMD -2.16), motor (aMD -1.40) composite scores; no difference on other 27 secondary outcomes
grade_reason: imprecision - trial authors state it may be underpowered for this signal
key_limitation: adverse secondary signal not a reassuring null - explicitly flagged by trial authors as possible true effect under-detected
notes: hPOD prophylaxis ITT effect; distinct from observational exposure analysis E10

author_year: Edwards 2022 (hPOD exposure analysis, JAMA Netw Open)
design: observational cohort analysis within RCT population (by hypoglycaemia exposure, not allocation)
n_events: 236 with neurosensory impairment (111 exposed + 125 unexposed, approx.)
population_detail: late preterm and term at risk, hPOD population
secondary_results: recurrent episodes NOT associated (19% vs 18%, aRR 1.06, 95% CI 0.63-1.80); lower Bayley cognitive (aMD -1.48) and motor (aMD -2.05) scores
rob_overall: moderate-high risk of confounding by indication (observational within RCT)
directness: direct population but observational design - confounded by indication (why prophylaxis failed)
grade_reason: risk of bias - confounding by indication, not a randomised comparison
key_limitation: apparent tension with CHYLD randomised null - methodologically not directly comparable, flagged not resolved
notes: Observational exposure analysis distinct from ITT prophylaxis effect E9; tension with CHYLD discussed in synthesis (d)
glucose_threshold_used: 2.6 mmol/L/47 mg/dL; severe <2.0 mmol/L/36 mg/dL; recurrent >=3 episodes

primary_result: no significant difference across doses vs placebo
effect_size: placebo 56% vs dextrose 45-50% depending on dose (aRD range -14% to -7%)
secondary_results: combined dextrose exposure: LOWER motor impairment (3% vs 14%, aRD -11%, 95% CI -19 to -3) and HIGHER cognitive scores (106.0 vs 101.1, aMD 5.4, 95% CI 1.8-8.9) - positive secondary signal, in tension with E9's adverse signal
grade_reason: imprecision (dose arms individually underpowered); tension with hPOD ITT result unresolved
key_limitation: positive secondary motor/cognitive signal not replicated in hPOD 2-year ITT (E9), which showed opposite direction - not adjudicated
notes: Dose-ranging prophylaxis trial, early school age
glucose_threshold_used: prophylaxis (no treatment threshold specified for this outcome)

design: observational cohort analysis within RCT population (by hypoglycaemia exposure)
secondary_results: severe or recurrent hypoglycaemia associated with worse visual motion perception and increased emotional-behavioural difficulty
rob_overall: moderate (observational within RCT, confounding by indication)
key_limitation: consistent with CHYLD dose-response pattern (severity/recurrence, not simple exposure, drives risk)
notes: Null primary result but dose-response on secondary outcomes, consistent with CHYLD pattern
glucose_threshold_used: 2.6 mmol/L/47 mg/dL; severe <2.0 mmol/L/36 mg/dL; recurrent >=3 episodes

outcomes_measured: neurodevelopmental impairment, visual-motor impairment, executive dysfunction (early childhood); impairment, literacy, numeracy (mid-childhood)
primary_result: null for global impairment (early childhood); positive for visual-motor and executive dysfunction
secondary_results: mid-childhood: impairment OR 3.62 (95% CI 1.05-12.42, n=54 only); literacy OR 2.04 (95% CI 1.20-3.47); numeracy OR 2.04 (95% CI 1.21-3.44) - in tension with later, larger, single-cohort CHYLD null (E3)
directness: mixed - pools term and preterm, at-risk and unselected populations across included studies
grade_reason: imprecision (n=54 for mid-childhood pooled estimate); inconsistency (superseded by later single-cohort null)
key_limitation: mid-childhood pooled estimate based on very small n and predates CHYLD's larger null result
notes: Cross-validates CHYLD's early-childhood domain-specific pattern; mid-childhood estimate should be read alongside, not instead of, the later CHYLD null
gestational_age_range: mixed across included studies (not specified in abstract)

n_events: not reported as single figure (moderate hypoglycaemia subgroup)
population_detail: unselected term singletons, diabetic mothers and NICU admissions excluded
outcomes_measured: any neurological/neurodevelopmental outcome; developmental delay; motor delay; cognitive delay, 2-6 years
effect_size: aOR 1.48 (any outcome); aOR 2.53 (developmental delay); aOR 1.91 (motor delay); aOR 2.85 (cognitive delay)
secondary_results: early hypoglycaemia (<6h) highest risk: aOR 1.94 (any outcome, 95% CI 1.30-2.89); aOR 3.17 (cognitive delay, 95% CI 1.35-7.43)
directness: indirect to CHYLD's at-risk cohort - this is an UNSELECTED population, largest sample in this domain
grade_reason: risk of bias (retrospective register, confounding by indication for testing not excludable)
key_limitation: cannot achieve CHYLD's dose-response granularity; large scale is main strength
notes: Rare population-attributable (not at-risk-only) evidence source in this domain
glucose_threshold_used: moderate hypoglycaemia (exact register threshold not given in abstract)

population_detail: children with neonatal glucose screening data, born 2010-2015, frequency-matched for sex/birthweight/GA/SES/risk factors
outcomes_measured: full-scale IQ; fine motor function; visual-motor integration; attention/ADHD symptoms, 7-11 years
primary_result: positive association with lower IQ and motor/visual-motor deficits
effect_size: IQ 107.0 vs 111.8 (4.8 points lower); fine motor OR 4.9; visual-motor integration OR 5.3
secondary_results: higher parent-reported attention-problem and ADHD-symptom T-scores in exposed group
ascertainment_method: retrospective glucose screening records, Wechsler/motor/visual-motor test battery at follow-up
directness: direct but uses a lower exposure threshold (<=1.7 mmol/L/30mg/dL) than the BAPM/CHYLD treatment threshold (2.6 mmol/L/47mg/dL)
grade_reason: risk of bias (retrospective recruitment, single centre); imprecision (n=140)
key_limitation: lowest exposure threshold in this domain - most relevant to 'what happens well below the treatment threshold' not to the treat-to-2.6mmol/L policy question
notes: Clearest, most consistent adverse IQ/motor signal in this domain, but at a much lower glucose threshold than current UK treatment threshold
gestational_age_range: not specified in abstract (implied term/near-term - severe asphyxia/other cerebral disease excluded as confound, not GA)

population_detail: >=35 weeks, BG<1.7 mmol/L (30 mg/dL) treated to >2.5 mmol/L (45 mg/dL); severe asphyxia/head injury/other cerebral disease excluded
outcomes_measured: Wechsler IV cognitive function; Movement ABC-2 motor function; Child Behavior Checklist, mean age 7.75-9.17y
primary_result: null for cognition and behaviour; positive (adverse) for fine motor function
effect_size: fine motor percentile 42.6 vs 57.2 (univariate); beta -16.4 for boys (adjusted)
secondary_results: no significant differences in Wechsler IV or Child Behavior Checklist
rob_overall: moderate (small n, sibling-control design partially addresses shared confounding)
grade_reason: imprecision (small n=71/32); mixed result across outcome domains
key_limitation: mixed result (null cognition/behaviour, positive fine motor) reported in full rather than reduced to single direction
notes: Sibling-control design; PMID 32794121 is a name-correction erratum for this same paper, not a separate study
glucose_threshold_used: <1.7 mmol/L / 30 mg/dL (exposure); treated to >2.5 mmol/L / 45 mg/dL

design: secondary analysis of multisite RCT cohort (historical, 1980s recruitment)
population_detail: PRETERM infants (Domain D population) - cross-referenced here as it bears on whether the term/late-preterm null pattern generalises
outcomes_measured: cognitive, academic, behavioural outcomes at 3, 8, 18 years
primary_result: null for cognitive/academic outcomes at all ages
effect_size: not a single pooled effect size (multi-age, multi-domain comparison)
secondary_results: more severe hypoglycaemia associated with FEWER problem behaviours at 18y - not judged clinically meaningful by authors
ascertainment_method: standardised cognitive/academic/behavioural batteries at 3 fixed ages
directness: PRETERM population but historical (1980s) glucose management practices differ substantially from current era - directness caveat applies both to gestation AND era
key_limitation: no dose-response detected at all, inconsistent with the term/late-preterm CHYLD severity/recurrence pattern - discussed in Domain D
notes: Preterm null finding; primary discussion in Domain D, cross-referenced here for the term-vs-preterm generalisability question
gestational_age_range: preterm (exact range not given in abstract; IHDP enrolled <=37 weeks and/or <=2500g historically)
glucose_threshold_used: 4 strata, exact cutpoints not given in abstract
